To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effect of the loading rate is different for concrete made with soft and hard aggregates.
the effect of strain rate on the behavior of concrete depends on the strength of the coarse aggregate and the confinement level.
the behavior of concrete under very high pressure is influenced by the type of aggregate used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of coarse aggregate strength on the mechanical behavior of concrete under static and dynamic QOC tests.
the effect of coarse aggregate strength on the behavior of concrete at high pressure and strain rate.
the effect of the type of coarse aggregate and strain rate on the static and the dynamic behavior of concrete.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the increase of concrete compressive strength with strain rate, as reported by several researchers, does not seem to be related to the strength of aggregates, but rather to their nature.
the increase of the strength of concrete with the strain rate depends on the strength of the coarse aggregates.
the behavior of concrete under dynamic compression is strongly dependent of the type of aggregate and its strength.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the behavior of concrete under very high confinement is influenced by both coarse aggregate strength and the loading path.
the effect of coarse aggregate strength on concrete strength at high pressure is more pronounced at high strain rate than at low strain rate.
the strength and deformation behavior of concrete under dynamic loading is highly sensitive to the type of aggregate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the strength of concrete is not only dependent on the strength of the aggregates, but is also dependent on the type of aggregates, the strength of the cement paste, and the strain rate.
the behavior of concrete under very high pressure is not only a function of the aggregate strength but is also dependent on its mineralogy.
concrete made with strong aggregates has a better response to dynamic loading.
